title: Sharp reset thresholds for bounded-response synchronization games with a sink
abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib statements of the theorem M(n,k) = sum_{i=1}^{n-1} ceil(i/k) for k = 1 or n <= k+3 (Lipin-Volkov k-game on automata with a sink), rendered as an upper and a lower bound, with the headline case M(5,2) = 6, proved in Solution.lean from the development SinkReset.Plan written in the conductor formalize run 2026-10-25_formalize-sinkresetthresholds. The endpoints k = 1 (Rystsov's tight bound n(n-1)/2) and k = n-1 were known from Lipin-Volkov; the new content is M(k+2,k) = k+2 and M(k+3,k) = k+4 for k >= 2, including the non-divisible pairs (4,2) and (5,3), which the Lipin-Volkov conjecture (stated for k | n-1 only) does not cover; (5,2) is the first pair with k | n-1 that is neither endpoint, i.e. the first pair on which the Lipin-Volkov conjecture itself was open ((4,2) is the first non-endpoint pair of all).
